reason: c1 (layout inversion risk) and c2 (group indexing by sorted position) — the two material correctness risks — are rebutted by end-to-end run-vs-reference GPU probes over the legal domain: 26 cases covering N not multiples of 64 (65,95,49,33,1), K not multiples of 16 or group_size (17,31,33,48,55,63,79,96,97,100,127), all group sizes {16,32,64}, M 1..65, shuffled and monotone g_idx, and adversarial negative high bits in qweight. All had 0 tolerance violations with max abs diff 8.4e-7 against a 0.01+0.001|target| tolerance — a ~4-order-of-magnitude margin. c3 (H16 decoded-weight rounding) is inconclusive solely because of repeated probe-construction bugs (uint16 arange/view not implemented), not kernel evidence. I set it aside as non-material: the fp32 product of the small integer (q−z) with an fp16-exact scale is exact in fp32, so the single .to(fp16) cast is arithmetically the contract's H16 round-to-nearest-even (the description model confirms this), and the end-to-end probes with arbitrary in-domain scales already passed with a huge margin. Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and recorded no new claims. No confirmed in-scope defect exists; the kernel correctly implements the canonical GPTQ INT4 projection contract.
